label: CSRD Sustainability-Data Impact Assessment
description: Assess how CSRD (EU) 2022/2464 and ESRS-mandated sustainability data feed investment analysis — valuation and screening inputs, SFDR (EU) 2019/2088 Art. 8/9 alignment and PAI indicators, greenwashing risk, and data-availability gaps across the portfolio.

claudeKnowledge.description: CSRD (EU) 2022/2464; ESRS Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 (ESRS 1, ESRS 2, E1–E5, S1–S4, G1); SFDR (EU) 2019/2088 + RTS Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1288 (Art. 8/9, PAI Table 1); EU Taxonomy Regulation (EU) 2020/852 + Disclosures Delegated Act; ISSB IFRS S1/S2; CSRD Omnibus simplification proposals (label as proposals); EFRAG ESRS implementation guidance; ESMA guidelines on funds' names using ESG terms; CSDDD (EU) 2024/1760

guidedInputs.label: Investor / User Role
guidedInputs.description: Whose perspective is this assessment from? Drives which disclosure obligations and data uses dominate.

guidedInputs.label: Portfolio / Asset Class in Scope
guidedInputs.description: What is being analysed? Determines ESRS data availability and the in-scope/out-of-scope reporter mix.

guidedInputs.label: Reporting / Domicile Jurisdiction(s)
guidedInputs.description: Which disclosure regimes govern the fund and its investees?

guidedInputs.label: Investment Use Cases for the Data
guidedInputs.description: How will ESRS/CSRD data be consumed? Prioritises which datapoints and gaps matter most.

options.label: SFDR Art. 8/9 product alignment & website disclosures
Valuation inputs (transition cost, carbon price, stranded-asset risk)

guidedInputs.label: Current Data Sourcing Model
guidedInputs.description: Where does the firm get sustainability data today? Shapes the data-availability gap and coverage estimate.

options.label: Third-party ESG vendor estimates only (e.g. MSCI / Sustainalytics / ISS)
Vendor data + issuer-reported ESRS where available

guidedInputs.label: Known Data Gaps or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Describe known coverage gaps, estimated-vs-reported tensions, greenwashing exposures, audit findings, or supervisory focus areas.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. ~40% of the small-cap sleeve are non-CSRD reporters so Scope 3 is fully estimated; an Art. 9 fund markets a 'net-zero aligned' label but ~half of holdings have no science-based target; ESMA fund-name rules force a relabel decision by Q4...

exampleInput: We run a EUR 1.2bn Article 9 European equity fund and an Article 8 multi-asset fund, both SFDR-classified in 2022. With the first wave of CSRD/ESRS reports now landing for FY2024, we want to understand how this newly mandated, assured sustainability data should change our valuation and screening inputs, and where it does NOT yet cover us. About a third of the Art. 8 sleeve sits in SMID-caps and private holdings that are out of CSRD scope, so their Scope 3 emissions and ESRS E1 transition-plan datapoints are still vendor-estimated. Run a sustainability-data impact assessment: map the ESRS datapoints we actually need for our SFDR PAI Table 1 reporting and EU Taxonomy alignment, assess the data-availability gap by holding type, flag where reliance on estimates creates greenwashing risk for our 'net-zero aligned' Art. 9 marketing claim, and tell us how transition costs and carbon-price assumptions from ESRS E1 should flow into our DCF assumptions. Known concern: our Art. 9 fund name uses 'sustainable' and we have not yet checked it against the ESMA fund-naming guidelines.

exampleValues.known_concerns: ~33% of the Art. 8 sleeve are non-CSRD reporters (SMID/private) — Scope 3 and ESRS E1 transition-plan data are fully estimated. Art. 9 fund markets a 'net-zero aligned' claim but a material share of holdings lack a validated science-based target. Fund name uses 'sustainable' and has not been checked against the ESMA fund-naming guidelines (effective for existing funds from 21 May 2025).
